purpose: Runtime/correctness pilot for sealed-bid target reliability under reference search vs the existing neural population. No training targets admitted from four worlds.
selection: One SHA-ranked later-round training bid root per count 2–6 and Original/Recharged; no observed outcome filtering. No development/confirmation/final positions used for fitting.

sizing.rationale: Same tested concurrency/hardware. Per arm, use the slower endpoint per game, double it for unseen deals/counts/opponents, and pack whole deals to a three-hour target. Never use pilot outcomes. This is a planning allowance, not a statistical bound.

candidate_actions: Unchanged current economic shortlist plus exact parent fallback, fixed before outcomes. No action selected for deployment.
paired_worlds: Same public-state seeded worlds across all candidate actions and both opponent populations; raw terminal scoring and shared-world hashes checked.
estimate_basis: Earlier exact-search diagnostic used about 85,247 aggregate CPU seconds for 896 reference plus 896 cheaper mixture continuations. Later-round roots should be shorter; target-host wall time remains provisional.
failure: Stop on first failure/cap; retain partial raw output; never resubmit automatically.
next_gate: Audit all ten roots and exact runtime cost. If sound, predeclare a larger disjoint-world target assessment before any bid-head training; four-world pilot scores are not action-quality evidence.
